correctness.rationale: The entire Hamiltonian splits into n local three-spin energies, with onsite terms shared equally because each edge of the cubic base has two ends. The complete ten-composition check gives six nonnegative-field candidate affine forms. A proper three-edge-coloring realizes any minimizing composition at every base vertex, giving equality and all-parameter quantifiers. Strict-minimum multiplicities are bijections with perfect matchings, three-edge-colorings, or unique uniform states. At D=J,h=0, allowed triangles are exactly 000 or -0+, hence vertex-disjoint even cycles with two signings per cycle. At D<0,h=4J, allowed triangles are exactly +++ or -++, hence arbitrary negative-edge matchings. Three complete-state finite verifiers and an independently coded graph-invariant census reproduce all specified examples; finite checks only supplement the proof.

value.rationale: The sharp all-field classification exposes a six-composition occupancy/magnetization diagram for a natural infinite kagome-like graph family, and exact degeneracies in terms of standard matching and edge-coloring invariants. It isolates two different coexistence combinatorics: weighted vertex-disjoint even cycles at the vacancy threshold and arbitrary matchings at the saturation threshold. These provide structurally useful exact residual-entropies for finite frustrated magnetic clusters rather than a routine graph relabeling or a single arbitrary numerical slice. Concrete cuboctahedral counts 69 and 108 make the distinction testable.
